_comment: Verdicts carried over from the source packs, keyed by the combined numbering.

1: Humidity forecast with its model comparison (SeasonalNaive, MAPE 1.9%). NOTE: this exact question declined on one of three attempts — the routing for it is not deterministic.
2: A 7-day building-wide electricity forecast was answered by a register decline. Per-floor electricity IS readable (see 8 and 17), so the data exists; the question did not reach the forecaster.
3: A real forecast: 192 hourly points of history, two candidate models scored on a 20% hold-out, and the better one (SeasonalNaive, MAPE 4.1%, R2 0.95) selected and named.
4: Honest decline: the atrium has no noise sensor. It says so, says this is what is recorded rather than a fault, and lists what the atrium does measure.
5: A floor-level temperature forecast was answered by a register decline. The single-room form of the same question forecasts correctly, so this is the floor-scoped shape failing, not the forecaster.
6: Answers the threshold question from the forecast rather than from the latest reading, and shows the model selection behind it.
7: Occupancy IS measured (511 series) and other answers use it, but this chart request found nothing to plot.
8: A week of temperature for one room, 160 readings. The 41.7 C peak it reports is worth asking the building about — the chart shows the system reporting what the sensor holds, not smoothing it away.
9: A chart drawn from the readings, with the reading in words beside it: low 508 ppm at 02:00, peak 1,030 ppm at 15:00, daytime 946 against nighttime 547.
10: Asked for humidity plotted AGAINST temperature; it charted temperature alone and dated the answer 2022. Two faults in one answer.
11: Six floors on one chart, 114 readings, with the peaks named per floor.
12: Ranks rooms on two constraints at once and shows the reading behind each (illuminance and noise), with a fit score.
13: Handles a weighted preference — noise first, daylight second — and shows both readings per candidate.
14: Ranks meeting rooms on CO2 AND occupancy together and shows both readings per candidate — the one cross-modal question that reaches the deliberation lane. It does not verify capacity for eight, which the workspace register holds.
15: Refuses to invent a "worst" verdict and says exactly which fields the register does hold. The right answer to a loaded question.
16: Live reading with its timestamp, plus the range over the last 60 records.
17: All six floors, highest and lowest identified.
18: Names the floor, the mean, the spread and the runners-up.
19: Now ranks rooms by live temperature and states how it read the question: "'coolest place to work' scored as minimize temperature against the 20-26 band". 'coolest' was in no lay-term list, so no measurand resolved and the workspace register answered instead; the model now resolves the word against this building's own concepts, and a resolved measurand takes a live superlative off a register lane. BUG-860 fixed.
20: Totals per floor and it names the six meters it summed.
21: A real comparison with its denominators stated: floor 1 over 574 readings from 14 sensors, floor 3 over 2,050 from 50.
22: States last week's per-floor totals are unavailable and gives this week's alone, so the comparison that was asked for is not made.
23: Gives per-floor means but never splits weekend from weekday, which was the whole question.
24: Now returns a ranking of rooms by temperature instead of declining, but the question asked for the largest WITHIN-FLOOR gap between warmest and coolest, and no gap is reported.
25: Comparing two modalities over time (CO2 rising while occupancy is flat) is not reachable: it declined and offered single-quantity questions instead.
26: Answered the outside-air half only. The delta-T across the heating circuit — the point of the question — is not in the answer.
27: "No readings were found for Floor_2" for a floor that answers elsewhere in this pack. A cross-modal question (ventilation against occupancy) reached a single-sensor lookup.
28: Says the building model records only how many sensors each space has and holds no current readings — which is false, and the opposite of what several other answers in this pack do.
29: A diagnosis question fell through to the generic capability decline.
30: Named anomalies with their room, modality, kind and severity.
31: Reports that 10 of 17 air-quality sensors appear in the recent window, which is adjacent to the question but does not say WHEN each one went quiet.
32: A completeness answer with the count, the number of distinct sensors, and the incomplete series named.
33: Says no calibration field exists. The 26-question pack answered the same fact (237 sensors overdue) from the building model, so this is a routing regression, not a missing record.
34: The building does distinguish measured from modelled records — this pack relies on that distinction — but the question reached the generic decline.
35: Correctly says it holds no evidence record for a previous answer in a fresh chat, and describes what one contains. The honest answer to a question with no antecedent.
36: Answers that no conflict-resolution rule is recorded and gives generic advice. The system does have precedence rules; it cannot describe them.
37: Re-derives the ranking with the temperature behind each candidate and a fit score, rather than asserting the earlier answer was right.
38: Declined on this run. The same question answered correctly on the previous run, with the freshest reading and its timestamp — one of six answers in this pack that differ between two identical runs.
39: Could not say which sources answered the previous turn — the provenance it publishes per answer was not reachable by asking for it.
40: Gives the date and distinguishes the room sensor from the general air-quality sensor.
41: 3 of 15 records, each with its id, permit kind and provider.
42: Splits fail-open from fail-locked with the device ids behind each.
43: Lists the assessments with their due dates and identifies the next one.
44: Overdue assets with location, due date and evidence reference.
45: Both overdue controls with their owner and due date, as at today.
46: 15 records split into closed, open and suspended, with each open permit's provider named.
47: Says plainly that no work order is recorded for floor 2, and that the register does hold the floor field — so absence means absence, not a gap in the query.
48: Lists the 9 open records AND states plainly that the register holds no due date, so 'overdue' cannot be derived from it. Refusing the second half of the question is the right answer.
49: Gives the count and the denominator it came from.
50: Both overdue controls with their due dates, as at today.
51: The target, its baseline, its deadline and its owner.
52: An energy-waste question declined, although per-floor and out-of-hours energy are both answerable here (8, 17, 40).
53: Names the systems running outside published hours and gives each one's exception status.
54: Answers 'not ready' and says which item is unevidenced, with the register and date behind each check.
55: Reads the room timetable as well as the ad-hoc bookings and names the session occupying the room. Before this change availability consulted bookings only, so a room carrying a weekly lecture reported itself free.
56: Direct answer against the booking window.
57: Answers, and marks the answer as the last known state with the age of the check rather than implying it is live.
58: Room count and total floor area from the floor-plan geometry.
59: The nearest accessible toilet is on the same floor, with the alternatives listed.
60: Lists the temperature sensors that ARE installed on floor 2; the question asked which rooms have none. A negation over the model is still not answered.
61: Lists the free bottle-filling stations, two per floor. The earlier capture named single placeholder points that had been dropped into arbitrary rooms.
62: Plan plus the spaces on the floor, grouped by kind.
63: Purpose, owner, operator, year and capacity from the building's own description.
64: Files the report, returns its id, category, priority and location.
65: Files it and asks for the location it could not determine, explaining why that matters.
66: Refuses to answer about an individual. NOTE: it refuses on the ground that energy cannot be attributed to a person, which is not quite the question asked; the refusal is right, its stated reason is off-target.
67: Says the cost register holds 24 records and none of them is a parking fee — absence located in a named register, not a shrug.
68: Refuses a blanket compliance claim and asks which regulation or record is meant. The only honest answer to that question.
69: Gives a defensible answer from the delta-T it can measure, says the plant is still performing, and recommends thresholds rather than pretending to a whole-life cost model.
70: Honest decline, and clearer than the previous run: it names the room and says there is no air-pressure sensor data for it.
71: States defibrillator positions and an emergency number as fact. The record behind it says the positions are 'modelled'. Safety-critical, so it must not be relied on until the owner confirms the three positions. Logged as BUG-858 (P1).
72: Declines, says a figure would be invented, and lists what IS measured there.
73: Refuses, states the refusal applies to every role, and offers the aggregate alternative.
